name: Greek Mythology
description: Olympians, Titans, heroes and the monsters they fought — plus their Roman names.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: Who is king of the Olympian gods and hurler of thunderbolts?
cards.fact: Zeus ruled from Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in Greece.

cards.prompt: Which god rules the sea and carries a trident?
cards.fact: Poseidon was also the god of earthquakes and of horses.

cards.prompt: Which god rules the underworld?
cards.fact: Hades was a brother of Zeus and Poseidon; the three divided the world between them.

cards.prompt: Which goddess of wisdom is the patron of Athens?
cards.fact: Athena was said to have sprung fully armed from the head of Zeus.

cards.prompt: Who is the goddess of love and beauty?
cards.fact: In one telling, Aphrodite was born from the sea foam off Cyprus.

cards.prompt: Which messenger god wears winged sandals?
cards.fact: Hermes also guided the souls of the dead to the underworld.

cards.prompt: Who is the Greek god of war?
cards.fact: Ares was so quarrelsome that even his father Zeus disliked him.

cards.prompt: Who is the god of wine and revelry?
cards.fact: Greek theatre grew out of festivals held in honour of Dionysus.

cards.prompt: Which god is the blacksmith of the gods, master of fire and the forge?
cards.fact: Hephaestus forged Zeus's thunderbolts and Achilles' armour.

cards.prompt: Which goddess of the hunt is the twin sister of Apollo?
cards.fact: Artemis and Apollo were born on the island of Delos to the Titaness Leto.

cards.prompt: Which goddess is queen of the gods and goddess of marriage?
cards.fact: Hera was both the wife and the sister of Zeus.

cards.prompt: Which harvest goddess is the mother of Persephone?
cards.fact: Demeter's grief while Persephone is in the underworld was said to cause winter.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Zeus?
cards.fact: The largest planet is named Jupiter, after the king of the gods.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Aphrodite?
cards.fact: Venus, the brightest planet in the night sky, carries her name.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Ares?
cards.fact: The red planet was named Mars for the colour of blood and war.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Hermes?
cards.fact: Mercury, the fastest-orbiting planet, is named after the swift messenger.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Poseidon?
cards.fact: Neptune, the deep-blue planet, fittingly bears the sea god's name.

cards.prompt: What is the Roman name for Athena?
cards.fact: Minerva's owl became a lasting symbol of wisdom.

cards.prompt: Which Titan stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity?
cards.fact: As punishment, an eagle ate Prometheus's liver every day, and it grew back every night.

cards.prompt: Which Titan was condemned to hold up the sky?
cards.fact: Books of maps are called atlases after him.

cards.prompt: Which Titan swallowed his children to stop them overthrowing him?
cards.fact: Zeus escaped when his mother Rhea gave Cronus a stone wrapped in baby clothes instead.

cards.prompt: Which hero performed the Twelve Labours?
cards.fact: Hercules is the Roman form of Heracles' name.

cards.prompt: Who slew the Minotaur in the Labyrinth of Crete?
cards.fact: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could find his way back out.

cards.prompt: Which hero beheaded Medusa?
cards.fact: Perseus watched Medusa only in the reflection of a polished shield.

cards.prompt: Who led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece?
cards.fact: His ship, the Argo, gave the Argonauts their name.

cards.prompt: Which Greek warrior's only weak spot was his heel?
cards.fact: In a later legend, his mother dipped him in the River Styx, holding him by the heel.

cards.prompt: Which king of Ithaca took ten years to sail home after the Trojan War?
cards.fact: Homer's Odyssey tells the story of his long voyage home.

cards.prompt: Which musician went down to the underworld to bring back Eurydice?
cards.fact: Orpheus lost her for ever by looking back before they reached daylight.

cards.prompt: Who flew too close to the Sun on wings of wax and feathers?
cards.fact: His father Daedalus, who built the wings, had warned him not to fly too high.

cards.prompt: Who opened a jar that released evils into the world, leaving only hope inside?
cards.fact: The original story has a jar; "Pandora's box" comes from a later mistranslation.

cards.prompt: Whose abduction by Paris sparked the Trojan War?
cards.fact: Helen's was "the face that launched a thousand ships".

cards.prompt: Which Trojan princess was cursed to prophesy truly but never be believed?
cards.fact: Cassandra warned the Trojans against the wooden horse, in vain.

cards.prompt: What is the name of the three-headed dog that guards the underworld?
cards.fact: Capturing Cerberus was the last of Heracles' Twelve Labours.

cards.prompt: Which many-headed serpent grew two heads for every one cut off?
cards.fact: Heracles' nephew Iolaus seared each stump with fire so no heads grew back.

cards.prompt: Which Gorgon turned anyone who looked at her to stone?
cards.fact: Medusa had living snakes for hair.

cards.prompt: Which winged horse sprang from Medusa's neck?
cards.fact: The hero Bellerophon rode Pegasus to defeat the fire-breathing Chimera.

cards.prompt: Who ferries the souls of the dead into the underworld?
cards.fact: Greeks buried the dead with a coin to pay Charon's fare.
